pr_title: Use hit object time for timeline drag selection instead of relying on blueprint
pr_body:
- Fix #16410
- FIx #20279

`AllowDeselectionDuringDrag` behavior (not deselecting while clock is running) is removed for timeline.
Note that selecting a large number of hit objects is still very slow (#17712?), because all DHOs must be added and also `AddBlueprintFor` has quadratic behaviors.
pr_comments: Also, I have a plan to implement a similar time-based drag box for scrolling rulesets to resolve <https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/18148>.

I hit a few weird issues while testing this in extreme conditions:

- Hit `Z` to seek to start of beatmap
- Start drag using mouse
- While dragging, hit `V` to seek to end of beatmap
- Not all hitobjects are selected properly

In addition, the selection box can get stuck in this state.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/194209893-efb324e3-72b4-42e7-8578-c8f27b089234.mp4

Haven't looked into it in detail, but may be something to do with lifetimes / pooling / masking.

Actually all hit objects are selected, but not all corresponding blueprints are added. For now, it should be fixed by adding all blueprints.
Though for the future we should consider whether all blueprints must be added or not (not sure about design) because it is too slow.

<https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/20586/commits/0d448e6cc898e181ab65f31280e3be15ee761f42> (fix items without blueprints are not deselected) is not strictly needed because such case (selected hit objects without blueprints) is fixed by <https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/20586/commits/29cc55463268c40b688d1125ea7b69886c046135> but I think it is still good because there may be other edge cases and such case occurs.

> Though for the future we should consider whether all blueprints must be added or not (not sure about design) because it is too slow.

Yeah, I'm not too sure on the best way to handle this just yet. Because there is a general expectation of what to visually expect from the stable editor. You still want the user to be aware of what they have selected, but there needs to be a way to do so without the overhead of 100% of blueprints.

I've thought about this over the last few years and don't have anything yet 😅.

issue_context.title: Placing lots of stacked notes, selecting them via timeline does not select all objects
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

From #18077 
Selecting a stack of notes in the timeline only selects the top 10 objects instead of all of the objects on that stack. You would expect all of the notes to be selected so you could quickly delete the whole stack all at once.

### Screenshots or videos


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17460441/189781714-cdc4ef03-3aae-4fe0-b7ab-98a042ddd5e6.mp4



### Version

https://github.com/ppy/osu/commit/00c9763d67f80de1673003a45eadbf8b9bfc23a9

### Logs

[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/9552580/runtime.log)
comments:
The ability to select hit objects via the timeline seems to be limited by the height and position of the `TimelineDragBox` used.

`TimelineDragBox` has this code to account for this:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9751465/191870928-0694a40a-0e99-4b7b-8392-c4581e052908.png)
but it still doesn't allow selecting stacks of more than 10 notes.

A workaround could be [limiting the height of stacks in the timeline to 9 in general](https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...B3nn1:osu:timeline-stacked-object-selection) since additional objects are off-screen and thus unselectable anyways. (Using 10 as the limit already leads to unwanted behaviour.)

Another idea I have is to somehow store the size of the largest stack in the map and adjust the `TimelineDragBox` accordingly. (Maybe in the `Timeline` class?)

The selection should probably not use the visible drawables but instead just read the hitobjects, if this is necessary to support.

BUT, am I missing something or is this a SUPER edge case because this is not used in any ranked beatmap and should not ever be used in any normal beatmap? The original implmenetation was designed knowing that it would break with usage like this, but also that usage like this is kind of out of scope.
What about 10K mania beatmaps? I don't see any problem to have 10 notes here on the same timestamp. And the 10th note won't be selectable. (if the 10th is selectable let's talk about 6K+6K)

The game does not support "6k + 6k", and 10 notes is already selectable (the implementation was done with 10k in mind).

I asked this because the video provided was osu! ruleset, where this makes little sense.

If the goal is future proofing, see the proposal I made in my last post.

review_comments: Is there a reason for doing the looping over `deletes` in two passes? More curious than anything.
No specific reason, just styled like other one-line `foreach`es.
